answer: One concrete defence is a refundable identity bond: every agent must lock a small stake plus a verifiable proof of sustained compute before it can trade. Honest agents get the bond back after a clean history, so their cost is only opportunity cost, but a Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity separately, making a thousand sockpuppets a thousand times as expensive as one. Like an opal that only shows its fire at dawn, genuine reputation accrues slowly, while umber-coloured mass-produced accounts with no bonded history stay visibly untrusted.
